chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Duke Ellington's interest in McRae and bass sax
summary: Duke wanted McRae for bass clarinet or bass sax, but he stayed with Chick; Ellington remembered what he heard and prized Mary Lou Williams.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Duke always wanted me to come into the band. He wanted -- after Ben had left, he wanted me way before the other fellow he had in there. His name as Al Sears.
All (inaudible), I (inaudible), "Well, Two and a half years// said I'm (inaudible). Duke, I'm with Chick," you know.
Even after I left Chick Webb, I used to go back to the Apollo Theater when Duke was appearing there.
I used to (inaudible) tell Johnny Hodges, "Hey, sign him up, sign him up, we'll get him in the band."
Now, I know what he wanted. He wanted me for my bass clarinet. He wanted to do something with the bass sax. He always liked that bass sax.
He always told me, "I want to do something with the bass sax. I want to do something.

You and CoAnley, we can do some great things together."
He had an idea if I came in on tenor playing bass sax -- bass clarinet -- that would leave CoAnley worrying about the bass clarinet.
He just (inaudible) bass -- a tenor, want a baritone and the clarinet. But he (inaudible) he bring me on the bass sax, because something he wanted, he heard us do.
I know he heard us play with Fletcher Henderson arrangement (inaudible). So great that Fletcher made for (inaudible) Coleman.
And Chick Webb had bought the arrangement for me, because, you know, we played (inaudible) Savoy. And he heard that.
And he always remember -- Duke always remember things, you know. He always remember things. He always remember Mary Lou Williams. He always looked at Mary Lou Williams as the greatest.
He always said, "You're the greatest." Mary wrote a thing (inaudible) for him, "Lady Be Good," a big arrangement. He always respected Mary Lou Williams for her talent. Mary Lou Williams was a great pianist,
